question: What standard cost-of-capital rate (WACC) did DHL Group apply across its divisions to compute the asset charge behind its EBIT after asset charge in fiscal year 2025, and was it changed compared with earlier years?
reference_answer: DHL Group applied a standard WACC of 8.5% across all divisions in FY2025 (this is also the minimum target for projects and investments in the Group). The rate was not changed: in 2025 it was maintained at a constant level compared with the previous years.

evidence.text: A standard WACC of 8.5% is applied across the divisions. That figure also represents the minimum target for projects and investments within the Group. … To ensure better comparability of the asset charge with previous figures, in 2025 the WACC used here was maintained at a constant level compared with the previous years.

question: How did DHL Group's EBIT after asset charge (EAC) change between fiscal year 2024 and fiscal year 2025, and what happened to the asset charge?
reference_answer: EAC rose from €2,207 million in FY2024 to €2,354 million in FY2025 (+6.6%). EBIT increased from €5,886 million to €6,103 million (+3.7%) while the asset charge rose only slightly, from €3,679 million to €3,749 million (+1.9%), so EBIT growth exceeded the rise in the asset charge.

question: DHL Group grew consolidated EBIT in fiscal year 2025. By how much did Group EBIT change, and which of the five operating divisions (Express, Global Forwarding Freight, Supply Chain, eCommerce, Post & Parcel Germany) reported lower EBIT than in 2024?

question: How did DHL Group's consolidated net debt change in fiscal year 2025, and which financing transactions were the main drivers of the increase in financial liabilities?
reference_answer: Net debt increased from €18,998 million at December 31, 2024 to €21,516 million at December 31, 2025. Financial liabilities rose from €24,209 million to €27,489 million, mainly because of bonds placed during 2025 with a total principal of €4.5 billion; the repayment of the 2017/2025 convertible bond (€1.0 billion) had an opposite effect.

evidence.text: Our net debt increased from €18,998 million as of December 31, 2024, to €21,516 million as of December 31, 2025.

Financial liabilities increased from €24,209 million to €27,489 million. The bonds placed over the course of 2025 with a total principal of €4.5 billion played a significant part in this. Repayment of the convertible bond 2017/2025 had an opposite effect of €1.0 billion.

question: How does DHL Group define free cash flow as a management indicator, how does it relate to free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures, and what changes in the management indicator from 2026?
reference_answer: Free cash flow (FCF) is a management indicator derived from operating cash flow (OCF); it indicates how much cash is available to the company for paying dividends or repaying debt at the end of a reporting period. In the Group's calculation, FCF = free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures ± cash inflow/outflow from acquisitions/divestitures. Starting from 2026, FCF will be replaced as a management indicator by free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures (FCF excl. M&A).

evidence.text: Free cash flow (FCF) is a management indicator derived from OCF. It is used as an indicator of how much cash is available to the company for paying out dividends or repaying debt at the end of a reporting period. Starting from 2026, free cash flow will be replaced as a management indicator by free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures (FCF excl. M&A).
FCF = Free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures (Free cash flow) ± Cash inflow/outflow from acquisitions/divestitures

question: How does DHL Group define its equity ratio and its net gearing ratio, and what were their values at year-end 2025?
reference_answer: Equity ratio = equity (including noncontrolling interests) divided by total assets; net gearing = net debt divided by the total of net debt and equity (including noncontrolling interests). At December 31, 2025 the equity ratio was 31.9% and net gearing was 48.7%.
